key_insight: The paper adds reason tags to preference-based reinforcement learning so the learned human reward model captures not just which trajectory is preferred, but why it is preferred.
engineering_relevance: This makes RL policies easier to align with human intent and safety expectations, while still improving task performance through reward shaping with human feedback.
method: Collect trajectory-level preference labels plus reason tags from humans.
Train a human reward model to predict preferences and the underlying rationale.
Combine learned human reward with environment reward during policy optimization to guide behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, compared with preference-only reward learning, the reason-guided approach improves human-aligned reward learning and policy interpretability.
watch_item: Reason tags add annotation overhead and may be inconsistent or noisy across annotators, which could affect reward-model quality.
paper_title: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
